question: A tall pea plant of unknown genotype is crossed with a pure homozygous dwarf pea plant (tt). Exactly 50% of the progeny are tall and 50% are dwarf. What was the genotype of the parent tall plant?
options: Heterozygous tall (Tt)
Homozygous pure tall (TT)
Homozygous dwarf (tt)
Triploid tall (TTT)
explanation: This is a classical test cross: Tt × tt. The gametes from Tt are T and t (50% each), and from tt are only t. The resulting offspring are 50% Tt (Tall) and 50% tt (Dwarf). If the parent were pure TT, 100% of offspring would have been tall.

Only 1 type of gamete (RrYy) at 100%

question: In garden peas, violet flower color (V) is dominant over white flower color (v). If a homozygous violet-flowered plant (VV) is crossed with a white-flowered plant (vv), what will be the flower color in the F1 generation?
options: 100% Violet flowers
100% White flowers
50% Violet and 50% White
Pink flowers
explanation: In Gregor Mendel's monohybrid cross with Pisum sativum (garden peas), pure-breeding violet-flowered plants (genotype VV) are crossed with pure-breeding white-flowered plants (genotype vv). The gametes produced are V from the violet parent and v from the white parent. In the F1 (first filial) generation, all offspring inherit the heterozygous genotype Vv. By Mendel's Law of Dominance, the allele for violet color (V) completely masks the expression of the recessive white allele (v). Therefore, 100% of the F1 progeny exhibit violet flowers. (NCERT Science Chapter 8, Section 8.2).

question: In birds, the mechanism of sex determination is ZZ-ZW. Male birds have two identical sex chromosomes (ZZ) and females have two different sex chromosomes (ZW). In birds, which parent determines the sex of the chick?
options: The father, identical to humans
Environmental nest temperature alone
The mother (female bird), because female ova carry either a Z or a W chromosome
The first hatched egg in the nest
explanation: In birds, the female is heterogametic (ZW) producing two types of eggs (50% Z and 50% W), while the male is homogametic (ZZ) producing only Z sperms. Thus, in birds, the female parent determines the sex of the offspring.

question: A father has blood group A (genotype Iᴬi) and a mother has blood group B (genotype Iᴮi). What are the possible blood groups of their biological children?

Only blood group A and B
All four blood groups are possible: A, B, AB, or O (25% chance each)
Only blood group O
explanation: The father produces gametes with Iᴬ and i; the mother produces gametes with Iᴮ and i. The four possible zygotic genotypes are IᴬIᴮ (group AB), Iᴬi (group A), Iᴮi (group B), and ii (group O), each with a 25% statistical probability.

question: In an asexual lineage, how can heritable DNA variations accumulate over successive generations?
options: All variations disappear after two generations
All variations revert to the original ancestor DNA
Only male offspring inherit variations
Descendants can inherit DNA changes already present in their parent lineage and may acquire additional changes through later DNA-copying errors
explanation: Asexual reproduction generally passes DNA from parent to offspring with high similarity. A heritable change present in a parent lineage can be passed to descendants, while new copying errors may introduce additional variation. Not every mutation is necessarily retained in every descendant branch.

question: Unlike male sperms which are of two chromosomal types (X or Y), all normal human ova (eggs) produced by a woman are chromosomally:
options: 50% carry Y and 50% carry X
Identical: 22 autosomes + one X chromosome (22 + X)
44 autosomes + XX
De-nucleated with no chromosomes
explanation: In human sex determination, chromosomes follow a strict XX-XY heterogametic system. Human somatic cells have 23 pairs (46 total) chromosomes: 22 pairs are autosomes and 1 pair is sex chromosomes. Normal human females possess two identical X chromosomes (genotype 44 + XX) and are strictly homogametic. During oogenesis meiosis, all mature ova produced receive an identical chromosomal complement of 22 autosomes and one X chromosome (22 + X). In contrast, human males possess one X and one Y chromosome (44 + XY) and are heterogametic, producing two distinct sperm types (50% with X, 50% with Y). Thus, the father's sperm uniquely determines the sex of the child. (NCERT Science Chapter 8, Section 8.3).

options: All alleles blend together like mixed paint
Dominant alleles destroy recessive alleles inside gametes
The two alleles of a gene pair separate during gamete formation so that each gamete carries only one allele for that trait
Alleles cannot separate once brought together
explanation: The Law of Segregation states that during meiosis, the two alleles of each gene locus segregate from each other so that each gamete receives only one allele with equal probability.

question: In the F2 generation of a dihybrid cross involving two independently assorting heterozygous parents (RrYy × RrYy), how many total squares (zygotic combinations) are represented in the Punnett checkerboard?
options: 16 squares (4 male gametes × 4 female gametes)
4 squares
8 squares
64 squares
explanation: In Mendel's dihybrid cross examining two independent traits simultaneously (seed shape and seed color), the F1 generation has genotype RrYy. By the Law of Independent Assortment, during gamete formation, the segregation of alleles of one gene pair is independent of the other, producing four genetically distinct gamete types in equal 25% proportions: RY, Ry, rY, and ry. When these gametes unite randomly during self-pollination, the Punnett square grid requires 4 columns * 4 rows = 16 zygotic boxes, yielding the classic 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio. (NCERT Science Chapter 8, Section 8.2).

question: Which seed color in pea plants is dominant, and which is recessive according to Mendel's experiments?
options: Green seed color is dominant; Yellow seed color is recessive
Yellow seed color is dominant; Green seed color is recessive
Both are codominant yielding striped seeds
Seed color in peas is completely random
explanation: In his foundational hybridization experiments on garden peas (Pisum sativum), Gregor Mendel investigated seven pairs of contrasting traits. For the trait of cotyledon (seed) color, Yellow seed color (designated by the capital letter allele Y) is completely dominant, while Green seed color (designated by the lowercase allele y) is recessive. A pea plant will produce green seeds only when it inherits two copies of the recessive allele in the homozygous state (genotype yy), whereas genotypes YY and Yy both develop yellow seeds. (NCERT Science Chapter 8, Section 8.2).

question: Which seed shape in pea plants is dominant, and which is recessive according to Mendel's experiments?
options: Wrinkled seed shape is dominant; Round seed shape is recessive
Oval seed shape is dominant over square seeds
Both round and wrinkled are dominant
Round seed shape is dominant; Wrinkled seed shape is recessive
explanation: Among the seven contrasting phenotypic traits studied by Gregor Mendel in garden peas (Pisum sativum), seed shape is governed by a single gene pair. The Round seed shape (designated by dominant allele R) is dominant over the Wrinkled seed shape (designated by recessive allele r). Wrinkled seeds lack the starch-branching enzyme (SBEI), causing higher sugar and water accumulation that shrinks upon maturation. Homozygous RR and heterozygous Rr plants produce round seeds; only homozygous rr produces wrinkled seeds. (NCERT Science Chapter 8, Section 8.2).

They blend into a single intermediate trait
They assort independently of one another
They are expressed only in male children
explanation: Under the stated model, genes on different chromosomes assort independently during meiosis. Human height is actually a complex, polygenic trait, so this question uses a simplified inheritance model rather than claiming that human height is controlled by one gene.
